answer:
**Out of full event sourcing; into an append-only ledger.** You get approx. 90% of the benefit at 20% of the cost.

**What billing actually needs** (all doable in plain Postgres):
- **Usage:** immutable raw events table w/ idempotency key, timestamp, customer, meter. Aggregate into rated line items; keep raw events so you can re-rate.
- **Money:** append-only double-entry ledger. Never update; correct via reversing entries or credit notes.
- **Invoices:** immutable once finalized, storing a snapshot of the pricing used.
- **Subscriptions:** normal state-machine table + history table of transitions.

**What full ES adds for a team of 4:**
- Event schema versioning & upcasting, forever.
- Projections, rebuild tooling, snapshots, eventual-consistency bugs (e.g. customer pays, UI still says unpaid).
- Harder debugging, ad-hoc queries & onboarding.
- GDPR deletion vs immutable log.
- Subscriptions are low-volume CRUD, so ES buys them little.

**Go full ES only if:**
- Someone on the team has run it in production before, &
- You must reconstruct arbitrary past state for regulators, or several downstream systems consume the same stream.

Excitement about the pattern isn't a reason; billing is the worst place to learn it.

**Prior question:** should you build at all? Stripe Billing, Orb, Metronome, or Lago (open source) cover subscriptions + usage. Build only if your pricing model is truly odd or billing is your product.
